claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with a few basic ones:

1. **How many children do you have that you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?** And what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 15 years old and lives with you at home.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! And just to confirm a few more details:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care?** For example, do you provide for their food, clothes, and other daily needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I take care of all their daily needs - food, clothes, everything they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, attending school, college, or an approved training program)

2. **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Alex is still at school - doing their GCSEs at the moment.

And no, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or are they claiming any benefits in their own right** (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're focused on their schoolwork. And they don't claim any benefits in their own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- ✓ You live in the UK
- ✓ Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
- ✓ You're responsible for Alex and they live with you
- ✓ You provide for Alex's daily needs
- ✓ Alex is in approved education (attending school doing GCSEs)
- ✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✓ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in their own right

You meet all the standard eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. You can proceed with making your claim!

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. Even if this applies to you, you can still claim Child Benefit - you would just need to pay back some or all of it through your tax return.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
